content.user_title: Organize Project Context With a Lightweight Workflow
content.value_statement: Projects can lose task context and development decisions between sessions. This playbook defines a small memory, planning, and logging workflow for consistent project work.
actual_capabilities: Defines a project-local .ai_context task record workflow.
Provides a short planning sequence with goals, constraints, steps, and validation.
Describes slash-first task dispatch using an optional manifest.
Recommends recording actions, changes, outcomes, and next steps.
Provides a beginner-focused welcome flow with three next actions.
limitations: It is a Markdown playbook, not a complete automation package.
Referenced scripts and reference files are not included in the scanned package.
It does not validate manifest contents or project-local scripts.
It does not replace project-specific security, testing, or review processes.

use_cases.title: Start a small repository workflow
use_cases.description: Create a minimal task record and plan before beginning a new repository task.

use_cases.title: Maintain session continuity
use_cases.description: Record completed actions and next steps so another AI session can continue the work.

use_cases.title: Port a lightweight process
use_cases.description: Adapt the documented context and dispatch pattern to an existing project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first task record
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a simple .ai_context task record for this goal: [goal]. Include constraints, up to five steps, and a validation method.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a focused change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the lightweight workflow to plan this change: [change]. List the goal, constraints, no more than five steps, and checks before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Record completed work
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise development log entry for this work: [work]. Include actions, changes, outcome, and next step.

prompt_templates.title: Review project dispatch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project manifest and propose a safe slash-first dispatch workflow. Do not run referenced scripts until I approve them: [manifest].

output_examples.input: Plan a documentation update for the installation guide.
output: Steps: review the guide, draft changes, verify commands, request review.
Validation: a new user can follow each step without ambiguity.

output_examples.input: Record that tests passed after updating a dependency.

best_practices: Inspect project-local scripts before approving their execution.
Keep task records concise and update them after meaningful work.
Define validation checks before changing project files.
anti_patterns: Do not run referenced helper scripts from an untrusted repository without review.
Do not store credentials or private keys in task records or logs.
Do not treat the manifest as a replacement for project documentation.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides a lightweight workflow for project context, planning, dispatch, and logs.

faq.question: Does it include runnable scripts?
faq.answer: No. The scanned package contains only documentation files and references scripts that are not bundled.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should I run the referenced Python commands?
faq.answer: Only after inspecting the project-local script and confirming its purpose and effects.

faq.question: Where does it store task context?
faq.answer: It describes a project-local .ai_context directory and active task record.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets?
faq.answer: No. Do not place secrets, credentials, or private keys in the context files or logs.
